newsitem.title: USA: Voters approve new Tampa, Fla., football stadium.
newsitem.headline: Voters approve new Tampa, Fla., football stadium.

text.p: Voters in Hillsborough County, Fla., narrowly approved a sales tax increase that will finance a new $168 million stadium for the Tampa Bay Buccaneers football team, elections officials said.
The measure passed with 53 percent of the votes cast in Tuesday's referendum.

The half-cent sales tax increase will raise $2.7 billion over 30 years. Twelve percent of the revenues will be used to pay debt service on a bond issue to finance a new stadium for the Bucs. The rest of the revenues would finance schools, roads, libraries and public safety projects, but the stadium received the most attention.

Tampa Mayor Dick Greco, who previously declared the proposal in trouble, held a jubilant news conference early Wednesday with Bucs' owner Malcolm Glazer, who had threatened to move the team out of Tampa unless voters approved the new stadium.
"We'll be able to plan for the future, something we've never been able to do," Greco said.

Hillsborough County Commissioner Joseph Chillura said passage of the hotly contested referendum was like "a halfback running through a minefield but the halfback got through the minefield and made a touchdown."
Former Tampa Mayor William Poe sued unsuccessfully in August seeking to have the referendum stricken from the ballot on grounds that it would use public money for private gain.
Smith Barney Inc was chosen last month as senior manager for the stadium bonds, to be issued by the Tampa Sports Authority.
